one_liner: Header-only PH-tree (bitwise Z-order quadtree) spatial map; about 5x faster inserts than Boost.Geometry's R-tree, slower kNN.
what_it_does: A multi-dimensional index (2 to 63 dimensions) over point or axis-aligned box keys with a std::map/std::multimap-like API: emplace, try_emplace with hint, find, erase, relocate/relocate_if, lower_bounds, window queries, kNN queries with Euclidean, L1 or Chebyshev distance, and custom filters (sphere, AABB). Map types (PhTree, PhTreeD, PhTreeF, PhTreeBoxD/F) hold one value per key; PhTreeMultiMap variants keep a bucket (std::unordered_set by default) per key. It is not a drop-in for boost::geometry::index::rtree: keys go through converter classes to int64, queries use for_each callbacks or iterators, and result accessors are first()/second() functions.
how_it_is_fast: The PH-tree (Zaeschke et al., SIGMOD 2014) is a bitwise prefix-sharing 2^DIM-ary trie: each node is a binary hypercube addressed by one bit per dimension, so entries sit in Z-order (Morton) order and a lookup or insert walks at most one path with bit arithmetic, no rebalancing. Insert/erase modify only one node (plus possibly one created or deleted), which is why updates are cheap; relocate() reuses the shared path when an entry moves a short distance. Node entry storage switches by dimension (fixed array_map for DIM<=3, sparse sorted vector up to 8, B+tree beyond), and traversal relies on count-trailing-zeros (TZCNT/BMI2) and AVX, hence the recommended -O3 -mavx -mbmi2. Doubles are mapped to int64 losslessly via their IEEE bit pattern by default.
when_to_use: Dynamic point sets with heavy insert/erase/move churn (simulations, game entities, moving objects) where an R-tree's rebalancing costs dominate; author's benchmark shows about 5x Boost R-tree insert throughput at 1M 3D points
Small window queries returning roughly up to 100 results per query, especially on clustered data (PH-tree 1.36x faster than Boost on 1M CLUSTER points)
Map semantics on exact coordinates (one value per key, find/count by point) with spatial queries on the same structure
Moderate dimensionality: the README says it works very well up to about 30 (sometimes 50) dimensions, with a hard limit of 63
Large datasets (millions of entries) built incrementally rather than bulk-loaded
when_not_to_use: kNN-heavy workloads: in the author's own 3D run Boost's R-tree answers k=1 queries about 13-26x faster at 1M points; there is no kNN for box keys at all (issue #36 open)
Box (rectangle) data with window queries: Boost R-tree is about 4.7x faster on 1M CUBE boxes in the same benchmark
Queries returning large result sets (the README says 1000+ results is inefficient; Boost already wins at about 100 results per query)
Static datasets that can be bulk-loaded once (packed R-trees or kd-trees such as nanoflann build fast and query faster)
Concurrent access: the README states the implementation does not support concurrency

integration.dependencies: none for the library (copy include/phtree); Bazel or CMake 3.14 only for tests, examples and benchmarks, which use GoogleTest and Google Benchmark
integration.min_toolchain: C++17; verified with GCC 12, Clang 14, Visual Studio 2022 (CMake) and AppleClang 14 (Bazel)
integration.platforms: Linux, Windows, macOS; x86-64 recommended with -mavx -mbmi2 for TZCNT (works without, slower bit iteration); benchmarks do not build on Windows
integration.thread_safety: not thread-safe: README says the current implementation 'doesn't support concurrency or serialization'; external locking required

gotchas: Map semantics: inserting a duplicate key silently does nothing (the FAQ calls this 'losing updates'); use PhTreeMultiMap or a set as value type
Iteration order is Z-order on the unsigned bit pattern, so negative coordinates come after positive ones; iterators are invalid after modification except as a hint after exactly one erase()

Correctness history: a heap-use-after-free in multimap relocate (vector reallocation in a node's sparse map, issue #153) was fixed in 1.6.2; issue #154 (bug, open since Aug 2023) reports a crash in the multimap test with NUM_DUPL=10 where emplace_hint after erase inserts at the wrong location
Lossy ConverterMultiply can speed indexes up by 10%+ but truncates coordinates; the default IEEE converter is lossless. Values are stored inside nodes, so store pointers for large objects
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick PH-tree over GeoToolbox KdBoxTree or nanoflann when the dataset changes constantly (insert, erase, relocate) rather than being bulk-loaded and queried, and over tidwall/rtree.c when you want a typed C++17 map API with up to 63 dimensions; pick nanoflann or Boost's R-tree instead when kNN or box queries dominate.
verified_claims_summary: In the author's separate phtree-cpp-perf repo (Google Benchmark, PH-tree 1.4.0 vendored, Feb-Mar 2023, GCC 12.1 and Clang 14, 8 x 4600 MHz CPU with 12 MiB L3, model unnamed), 3D inserts at 1M entries run at 2.79M/s vs 500k/s (points, CUBE) and 1.44M/s vs 406k/s (boxes) against Boost.Geometry's R-tree, about 3.5-5.6x; window queries are mixed and Boost wins box queries (about 4.7x) and 3D kNN (about 13-26x).
status_note: Maintained by the original PH-tree author as a fork of Improbable's abandoned repo; last commit 2026-03-19 but the last release is v1.7.0 (GitHub release dated March 2024; CHANGELOG header says 2025) with 14 open issues, so slow-moving; Apache-2.0 and header-only, easy to vendor.
